deficiencies.description: The rewrite inserts 'that is', asserting that acetylation or deacetylation is the same thing as the state of transcription, which the lecturer did not state.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: to the acetylation or deacetylation, the state of the transcription within the cell itself.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: and to acetylation or deacetylation, that is, the state of transcription within the cell itself.
deficiencies.studentHarm: A student would wrongly learn that acetylation or deacetylation is identical to or defined as the state of transcription, rather than being a chromatin modification that influences transcription.

deficiencies.description: The rewrite broadens the cause of predisposing to chronic inflammatory events from the specific human viruses ('they') to 'infection' in general.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: There are about seven different human viruses that will precipitate cancer, and they can also predispose to chronic inflammatory events that can also help to give rise to cancer.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: There are about seven different human viruses that precipitate cancer, and infection can also predispose to chronic inflammatory events, which can also help to give rise to cancer.
deficiencies.studentHarm: A student would learn that infection in general predisposes to chronic inflammatory events in this context, rather than the specific oncogenic human viruses described by the lecturer.
